chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammaad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, who said:

The first time I recognized Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was when I saw a man enter from the Door of al-Feel and prayed four cycles. So I followed him until he came to the Well of Zakat, which is near the house of Salih ibn Ali, and there were two camels tied up with a black slave with them. So I said to him, 'Who is this?' He said, 'This is Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' So I approached him, greeted him, and said to him, 'What brought you to a land in which your father and grandfather were killed?' He said, 'I visited my father and prayed in this mosque.' Then he said, 'Here is my face. May Allah send greetings upon him.'

key_terms.بَابُ الْفِيلِ: The Door of al-Feel (a gate in Mecca)
key_terms.بِئْرَ الزَّكَاةِ: The Well of Zakat (a well in Mecca)
key_terms.زُرْتُ أَبِي: I visited my father (referring to Ziyarat of Imam Ali or the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What was the first time Abu Hamza recognized Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the reverence of early companions like Abu Hamza for Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), illustrating the practice of Ziyarat to the Prophet's family in Mecca. The Imam’s response, pointing to his face as a representation of his father, underscores the Shia theological concept of the Imam as the living embodiment of the Prophet's legacy and spiritual presence.
